source: data/emails.md: Inbox accounts@harbourline.co.uk, Suppliers / September 2026, exported 2026-09-30 08:05, twelve messages, oldest first
conventions: One record per message: 12 messages, 12 records. One invoice number can have several records (original, correction, duplicate copy, void notice); see documents for the standing state of each number.
Money is a number with two decimals in the record's own cur. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD. gross = net + vat was checked on every record that has amounts. Every GBP invoice carries VAT at 20%.
flags use the legend codes. PAID, REFUNDED, POVAR and NOPO are deliberately not set: they need the bank feed and the PO list, which are not mine.
Nothing here is a pay, hold or exclude decision. That is the reconciler's.
limits: The export holds message bodies only. Where a message says an invoice or credit note is attached, the attachment is not in the export; every figure comes from the body text.
All 12 messages are dated 2026-09-02 to 2026-09-28, inside the 2026-09-30 receipt cutoff (policy 1).

sender_addresses.note: same address the invoice body gives for questions
Lookalike on inbox evidence: domain northfield-print.co, while all five other Northfield messages use northfield-print.co.uk. Not compared with the supplier master (not mine).

Policy 8: an email is never sufficient; a change needs the principal's approval and a call-back on the number on file; until then pay to the details on file. Policy 9: agents do not reply to or phone suppliers, so the call-back is the principal's.

Escalated to the principal as extractor-01 (options DECLINE or CALLBACK). The principal answered DECLINE (human-02): do not update the details, pay Northfield to the details on file, the principal will call the number on file, treat the .co email as suspected fraud. Relayed to the reconciler as extractor-12, at its request (reconciler-13). Payments to Northfield are not held up by this.
